steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly grease an 8x4 inch loaf pan.
In a large bowl, cream together butter and sugar. Beat in the egg and mashed bananas. Mix in flour, baking soda and salt just until combined. Pour into prepared loaf pan.
Bake in preheated oven for 1 hour. If top begins to brown too quickly, decrease heat slightly. Center should be soft and chewy, while the outside, crisp and crunchy.

raw_recipe.headline: Janine's Best Banana Bread
raw_recipe.description: Ripe bananas are the key to this sweet, no-frills delight. Hidden inside its sweet, slightly crunchy crust is soft and chewy banana goodness.
raw_recipe.name: Janine's Best Banana Bread

review.reviewBody: Review update - after making many batches of this wonderful bread, I finally think I figured out where the "dry" reviews are coming from. The bananas I used before were quite large. The bananas this time were not as big and I only had the 3. The batter turned out much stiffer than usual and I got a very dry loaf. So use BIG bananas, or add extra if you have smaller bananas. I guess a cup amount would be more accurate.
Excellent! I added a handful of brown sugar (a trick my mom taught me for color and a nice crunch to the crust) and a dash of milk to thin it out a little.

I've made this recipe exactly as written and been VERY happy. So my rating is totally legitimately for the exact recipe. However I most often do half white/half brown sugar as one reviewer suggested and I like it. The crust has a nice texture to it and soft bread on the inside.

Here are some variations I do. One thing I've done is to throw in a cup of chocolate chips. Usually I bake these in muffin tins rather than a loaf pan. I usually get 12-18 muffins and bake at 350 for 20ish minutes. This morning we tried something new. My mom used to make Taste of Home's banana split muffins and I wanted to try doing something like it for a change of pace. We did the half white/half brown sugar, I used 4 bananas because I had them, threw in half or so a can of crushed pineapple (I had some leftover in the fridge I wanted to use up), 1/2 cup of sweetened shredded coconut, 1 cup of chocolate chips and it made 18 muffins. SO GOOD. I loved it and the kids seemed to as well. Will absolutely be trying this again sometime.

I substituted 1/2 cup xylitol and 2/3 c up packed brown sugar for the 1 cup sugar. I also substituted 1.5 cups of oat flour for 1 of the cups of all purpose flour. I added 2 tsp vanilla and a scant pinch of cinnamon and nutmeg each. I also added 1 TB sour cream and 1 TB plain Greek yogurt and 1/2 tsp baking powder. Baked in a clay bread pan for 75 minutes at 370* as it was still not a clean toothpick at 1 hour. Yum!
Not bad! I like to add a capful of vanilla extract and an extra banana to keep it moist and make it taste better. If you make yours in a muffin tin, cook them for about 20-25 minutes at 320 degrees.

I've made this too many times to count, and each time it gets rave reviews. I like to use this recipe for muffins. I preheat the oven to 350 but turn it down to 325 for the bake. Add 1/4 tsp baking powder to the dry ingredients and stir in 1/2 c chocolate chips at the end. This recipe works great with herbal butters.

Omg this bread is delicious!!! I took advice from some other comments and did 2 eggs, 4 bananas, 1 tsp vanilla extract. I also did 3/4c white sugar and 1/4c brown sugar. I split this recipe into two smaller loaves and cooked for about 35 mins. I’ll definitely be making this again!
I add a little more butter at the beginning and an extra egg but over it is very good. I also cook in mini loafs so it cooks more even. 20-25 min at 350.

I made this recipe tonight but because I had several bananas that were given to me by a friend, I doubled the recipe and made a bunt size cake. In doubling the recipe I added 2 extra bananas for a total of 8 ripe bananas. I substituted 2/3 cup of brown sugar for the same amount of white sugar to get a somewhat crispy crust. I added some cinnamon to the batter and about 1 tsp. of vanilla. I must say, I have made banana bread before, but this one was nice and moist and slightly crispy crust on

I just made it and after reading a lot of recipes, I added a 1/2 tsp of cinnamon and a 1/4 tsp nutmeg. When I put it in loaf pan, I melted 2 Tbs butter, poured it on top, then added crumbled brown sugar all over before I baked it. OMG, sooo yummy!!

I doubled the recipe, did only 1 & 1/2 cups of sugar, and completely eliminated the salt because I thought there was enough baking soda for salt. Turned out DELICIOUS!!! Might be the best banana bread I’ve ever made! Small but delicious crunch on the top and soooo soft and moist in the middle. I highly recommend!
Excellent recipe but I really wish folks would include all countries weighs and measures in their ingredients.
Yummy
Easy to follow. Comes out of the oven with a sweet somewhat crusty exterior. Super moist inside. This doesn’t last long!
I get so many compliments every time i make this. i adjust the flour and add vanilla
Easy, not many ingredients, very tasty!
I added a bit of brown sugar, an extra egg, and some milk because the dough was way too thick. It came out great!
Can’t keep this stuff in the house. I add nuts, extra banana, brown sugar, cinnamon, vanilla, and sour cream. Sprinkle loaf top with additional brown sugar prior to baking. Super good!
I followed the recipe but added some chopped chocolate chips. Still seems it could be a little sweeter... may add some extra sugar or brown sugar next time.
So easy to make and such a great recipe 😋
